title: Preregistered Paired Evaluation of a Deterministic Verifier Pipeline for LLM‑Generated Network Configuration Changes — Non‑informative / Testability Failure under Shared‑Generation Semantics
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (cand-2026-01-prereg-v1) that tested whether a deterministic verifier pipeline (generate → deterministic_netops_validator_v5 → optional repair) reduces the rate of verifier‑detected unsafe intent→configuration proposals produced by a hosted LLM. Design: N=200 preregistered unique intent→configuration tasks in a paired design comparing (a) baseline LLM‑only and (b) guarded pipeline (declared model gpt-5-mini). Execution used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (one LLM call per task) to conserve model budget; model_calls_used = 200. Observed (adversarial cluster): baseline SAFE = 200/200; guarded SAFE = 200/200 (paired contingency n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0). Estimated paired SAFE‑rate difference = 0.0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (resamples = 10,000, seed = 1729). Because identical per‑pair candidates were produced and no repairs were applied, the preregistered causal hypothesis (that the deterministic verifier reduces unsafe proposals) was not testable in this execution. We publish the completed preregistered run and artifacts, provide an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of this testability failure, and give concrete, archive‑supported recommendations (independent per‑arm generation budgeting, adversarial calibration using a reserved exploratory set, pilot contingency checks, and alternative estimands) to enable informative repeats.

sections.introduction:
Motivation and research question. Translating operator intent into device configuration is a high‑impact NetOps task where errors (misordered changes, missing dependency steps) can cause outages or security exposures. Tool‑augmentation—pairing large language model (LLM) generators with deterministic validators or sandbox simulators in generate–validate–repair pipelines—has been widely proposed to reduce risk. We preregistered a confirmatory paired experiment (cand-2026-01-prereg-v1) to answer a focused causal question: under controlled synthetic NetOps tasks, does adding a deterministic verifier decrease the rate of verifier‑detected unsafe proposals produced by a hosted LLM? The preregistered primary estimand was the paired SAFE‑rate difference (guarded minus baseline) tested with an exact McNemar two‑sided test and a paired bootstrap CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729).

Contributions. (1) A complete, deterministic, preregistered paired run (N=200 paired tasks) executed and archived under the declared model gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, including full validator traces and analysis artifacts; (2) an artifact‑grounded diagnosis explaining why the executed run was non‑informative for the preregistered causal estimand (shared generation semantics + validator labeled every sampled candidate SAFE + no repairs applied); (3) concrete, archived‑supported recommendations for repeatable, informative confirmatory designs (independent per‑arm generation budgeting, exploratory adversarial calibration, pilot contingency checks, and alternative estimands when budgets constrain independence). The paper emphasizes reproducible methodological lessons rather than claiming production safety.
sections.related_work: Prior surveys and prototype reports document rapid adoption of LLMs for NetOps tasks (intent translation, configuration synthesis, diagnostic assist) and repeatedly recommend verifier/simulator augmentation to guard execution risk [Bilal et al., 2026; Fan et al., 2025]. Empirical and methodological studies show generate–validate–refine (or divide–verify–refine) pipelines can reduce explicit constraint violations on curated tasks, but measured gains depend strongly on verifier fidelity, task sampling semantics, and generation/repair budgeting [Zhang et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Several recent works advocate workflow‑centred, replayable, sandboxed evaluations and ROC‑style diagnostics for verifier behaviour to capture both false negatives and false refusals when guardrails are applied [Tarun Yadav, 2026; Ferrag et al., 2026]. Red‑teaming and guardrail research in adjacent domains highlights that adversarial templates and calibration are necessary to stress test guardrails and to avoid false confidence from insufficiently challenging benchmarks. Our study aligns with these calls by preregistering a paired estimand, using deterministic synthetic task generation, and archiving validator traces for deterministic replay; it addresses an empirical gap identified in the literature: reproducible, preregistered adversarial NetOps experiments that quantify the paired causal effect of adding a deterministic verifier under explicit generation semantics [Zhang et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026; Ferrag et al., 2026].
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as cand-2026-01-prereg-v1. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (guarded − baseline) on binary SAFE indicators produced by the deterministic sandbox validator. Confirmatory test: exact two‑sided McNemar implemented by paired_binary_analysis_v1; paired bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). The preregistration prespecified N=200 paired tasks (planned paired episodes = 400), sampling rules, an exclusion/missingness policy, and a power plan target (detect ~7 percentage‑point paired reduction with ≈80% power assuming baseline unsafe rate ≈10–15%).

Task generation, scope, and seeds. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 200 synthetic intent→configuration tasks constrained to single‑AS multi‑device topologies and limited configuration fields (admin, mtu, vlan). Generator seeds and per‑task generation_seed values were preregistered to ensure replayability. Tasks included explicit initial_state, expected_final_state, and per‑task workflow policies (required_sequence). The preregistration also defined a cluster of adversarial prompt transforms to increase difficulty and reserved up to 50 exploratory tasks to calibrate adversarial strength before confirmatory execution.

Compared pipelines and generation semantics. Baseline: post hoc scoring of the LLM candidate with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (no runtime enforcement). Guarded: deterministic validation of the same candidate in a sandbox using deterministic_netops_validator_v5; per the preregistration, the guarded arm could optionally apply one automatic repair call. Critically, the preregistration allowed two generation semantics: (A) independent per‑arm generation (one LLM call per arm per task) or (B) shared_initial_candidate (one shared LLM call per task scored by both arms). The executed run used shared_initial_candidate to conserve hosted model budget (execution choice recorded in model configuration); this choice reduces model calls but also constrains the possible discordance between arms.

Model, execution, and scoring. Declared model: gpt-5-mini. Execution adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 harness. Executed model_calls_used = 200 (one shared call per task); planned maximum_model_calls for independent per‑arm generation = 400. Deterministic_netops_validator_v5 applied full_intent_constraint_validation and emitted deterministic valid flags, violation lists, and structured validator traces; confirmatory binary outcomes derive from validator.valid (1 = SAFE, 0 = UNSAFE). Analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 to produce contingency counts, an exact McNemar p‑value, and paired bootstrap CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). Missingness and retry rules were applied as preregistered (one automatic retry per failed call; contaminated or nondeterministic tasks excluded and replaced). Deterministic reconciliation and provider audit checks were run as preregistered.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The execution manifest reports completed_episode_count = 400 (200 paired episodes), failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 200, consistent with shared_initial_candidate semantics and with no recorded technical failures or exclusions. Provider audit recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and no cross‑condition cache reuse. The exploratory reserve (up to 50 tasks) was not consumed before confirmatory execution.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. The deterministic validator labeled every sampled candidate SAFE: baseline SAFE successes = 200/200 and guarded SAFE successes = 200/200. Contingency counts: n11 = 200 (SAFE in both arms), n10 = 0 (SAFE guarded only), n01 = 0 (SAFE baseline only), n00 = 0 (UNSAFE in both). Paired SAFE‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (resamples = 10000; bootstrap_seed = 1729). All statistical outputs are direct products of paired_binary_analysis_v1 and are archived in the analysis artifacts.

Representative validator traces and repairs. Representative scoring JSONs show that for multiple tasks the shared_initial_candidate content is identical for baseline and guarded episodes; validator traces report validation_before and validation_after with violation_count = 0 and valid = true in every confirmatory episode. repair_provider_trace fields are null in confirmatory scoring JSONs, confirming that no automatic repair was invoked during these episodes and that the guarded arm performed only validation (no candidate alteration).

Why the inferential test was uninformative (diagnostic paragraph required by design). The preregistered paired causal contrast depends on discordant pairs (n10 or n01) that can arise only if (a) the baseline and guarded arms observe different candidates (independent per‑arm generation), (b) the guarded arm deterministically repairs an unsafe candidate to a safe one (producing discordance), or (c) the validator behaves nondeterministically across repeated replays. In the executed run the following archived facts jointly occurred: (1) shared_initial_candidate semantics (one LLM call per task, shared across arms); (2) deterministic_netops_validator_v5 labeled every candidate SAFE (baseline SAFE = 200/200); and (3) no repairs were applied (repair traces null). These three conditions mechanically preclude discordant pairs and therefore render McNemar‑style inference uninformative for the causal estimand. The observed p = 1.0 and degenerate CI [0.0, 0.0] reflect this testability failure rather than evidence of the guarded pipeline’s efficacy in broader or adversarial contexts.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and operational implications. The ceiling outcome (all SAFE in both arms) does not demonstrate that LLM proposals are safe in production; instead, it shows that under the executed semantics and the sampled tasks there was no arm‑level variation to attribute to the verifier. The preregistered power calculation assumed a nonzero baseline unsafe rate (~10–15%) and sufficient discordant probability mass (e.g., paired discordance p10+p01 ≈ 0.08) to detect a ~7 percentage‑point paired difference with N≈174. Those assumptions were not met because shared generation semantics constrained per‑arm stochasticity and the explored adversarial templates did not elicit unsafe outputs for the declared model on the sampled synthetic tasks.

Artifact‑grounded recommendations for informative repeats. All recommendations follow directly from the preregistration and archived execution accounting:
- Independent per‑arm generation for confirmatory paired contrasts: to test the causal effect of a verifier, allocate independent model calls per arm (preregistered independent generation requires ~400 model calls vs the executed 200), or ensure the guarded arm will deterministically alter candidates via repair so discordance can arise.
- Use the preregistered exploratory reserve (up to 50 tasks) to calibrate adversarial transforms until the baseline unsafe rate approximates power assumptions; archive these tuning runs and freeze transform parameters before the confirmatory run.
- Implement a preregistered pilot contingency check (small holdout) and abort the full confirmatory run if pilot contingency shows ceiling/floor counts; follow predetermined contingency‑preserving adaptation paths (enable independent draws or increase adversarial strength) rather than proceeding to an uninformative confirmatory test.
- When budgets preclude independent draws, switch the estimand to one testable under shared semantics (e.g., estimate absolute baseline unsafe rate with CI, or treat the guarded arm as an accept/reject gate and quantify refusal and post‑repair SAFE rates). The preregistration already declared such secondary estimands and exploratory diagnostics.

Threats to validity and scope. Construct validity: synthetic tasks limit field coverage to admin/mtu/vlan and single‑AS topologies; deterministic validator completeness relative to production failure modes is limited. Internal validity: using shared_initial_candidate removes arm‑level stochasticity and can produce mechanical ceiling/floor effects when candidate validity is high. External validity: single‑model scope (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic topologies restrict generalization to multi‑vendor, multi‑AS production networks. Conclusion validity: the absence of discordant pairs prevents a meaningful test of the preregistered paired estimand in this execution.

Practical operator trade‑offs. Independent per‑arm generation increases model‑call cost but is necessary to test causal effects when repairs are not guaranteed to induce discordance. Calibrating adversarial strength requires upfront exploratory expense but is essential to avoid underpowered or untestable confirmatory executions. Our archived artifacts quantify the concrete resource arithmetic (200 vs 400 model calls) and provide deterministic traces operators can examine when choosing budgets versus inferential goals.
sections.conclusion:
We executed a fully archived, preregistered paired experiment comparing gpt-5-mini baseline generation and a deterministic verifier‑augmented pipeline on 200 synthetic NetOps tasks. Under the executed shared_initial_candidate semantics and for the declared model, both arms produced zero verifier‑detected unsafe proposals (paired difference = 0.0; exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]). Because identical per‑pair generations were used and no repairs were applied, the preregistered causal hypothesis was not testable in this run. The scientific contribution is therefore methodological and reproducibility‑centred: (1) a complete deterministic preregistered run with archived artifacts that permit exact replay; (2) an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of why this execution was non‑informative for verifier efficacy (shared generation semantics + validator labeled every candidate SAFE + no repairs); and (3) concrete, archive‑supported recommendations (independent per‑arm generation budgeting, adversarial calibration via exploratory reserve, and pilot contingency checks) to enable informative repeats. Practitioners should choose generation semantics and budgeting that make their chosen estimand testable; the archived artifacts permit deterministic replay and pre‑execution pilot checks to avoid repeating uninformative confirmatory tests.

Validator and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performed deterministic sandboxed validation and emitted binary labels (1 = SAFE, 0 = UNSAFE) under scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation; archived scoring JSONs contain validator traces showing validation_before/after and violation lists. Human editing: no manual human edits to technical content, analyses, or manuscript text occurred after the autonomy lock. Pre‑lock development: infrastructure rehearsals occurred prior to the lock but were excluded from final empirical evidence unless reproduced under the post‑lock execution.
limitations: Synthetic tasks and scope: tasks were deterministic synthetic topologies produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and limited to single‑AS, multi‑device setups; results may not generalize to production, multi‑AS, or vendor‑specific features.

Generation semantics: the executed run used shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false), producing identical per‑pair generations and creating a ceiling effect when shared candidates were valid.

Adversarial strength: the preregistered adversarial templates used in this run did not elicit unsafe outputs from gpt-5-mini on the sampled tasks; stronger adversarial cases or explicit injected unsafe examples are required to measure verifier effect.
Single‑model scope: only the declared model (gpt-5-mini) was evaluated; no multi‑model generality is claimed.

Verifier completeness: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 ran deterministically in synthetic sandboxed states; external validation of validator completeness against all real‑world NetOps failure modes is not provided.

Operational external validity: no production deployment, operator‑in‑the‑loop workload measurement, nor multi‑vendor field trials were performed; operator‑cost trade‑offs remain unquantified at scale.
